title: Retinal ganglion cells · electrical stimulation
recordingType: Measured, spike-sorted ex-vivo mouse retinal recordings
licenseAppliesTo: Source data and adapted excerpt data
citation: Höfling L, Zeck G (2021). CMOS-MEA recordings of mouse retinal ganglion cells upon smooth electrical stimulation. G-Node. doi:10.12751/g-node.0blveb. Related paper: Höfling L, Oesterle J, Berens P, Zeck G (2020), Scientific Reports 10:5248, doi:10.1038/s41598-020-61899-y.
device: Multi Channel Systems hdCMOS-MEA 5000 research array
processing: Source recordings were processed by the authors for stimulation-artifact removal and spike sorting.
For each of two released .cmtr files, retain all units with empty Tags and peaks marked IncludePeak by the source sorter. No extra reliability or inter-spike interval exclusion is applied.
Select accepted timestamps in the first 20 seconds [0,20000000 microseconds); count spikes in nonoverlapping 10 ms bins using integer timestamp arithmetic.
Original accepted spike timestamps are also retained as integer microseconds and seconds. No synthetic spike times, voltage reconstruction or additional smoothing is used.
limitations: These data were recorded ex vivo from mouse retinal tissue on an hdCMOS-MEA 5000. They were not recorded by PRIMA, Argus II, or another clinical retinal implant.
Sorted units estimate neuronal spike trains; counts are not electrode voltage, and the excerpt does not include the delivered stimulation waveform or exact stimulus event timestamps.
The wildtype and rd10 examples come from different sessions and preparations. They are illustrative examples, not a matched experiment or a device-performance comparison.
Source row/column values identify sorter-assigned recording-grid locations. They are not clinical implant contact coordinates or precisely reconstructed soma positions.
This excerpt does not apply the published paper’s reliability-selection criteria, so it must not be presented as reproducing the paper’s response statistics.
